answer: Persistent kernel-time anchoring. Each identity must continuously answer a unique, stateful computational challenge whose solution evolves from the prior round, forcing serial work on one kernel instance. A shared echo of the last verified state is published per round, and any duplicate replay from a cloned agent is rejected at the jetty before admission. Attackers pay one full round of uninterrupted compute per identity, so N sybils cost N sequential workloads rather than N cheap registrations.
